walkthroughs.body_html:
The Brain and Neuropsychology — a core area of GCSE Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Brain and Neuropsychology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Brain and Neuropsychology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The brain and spinal cord together form the:
options: PNS
CNS
ANS
Somatic system

mcqs.q: Fight-or-flight is triggered by which nervous system branch?
options: Parasympathetic
Sympathetic
Somatic
Central

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Autonomic nervous system”?
options: Specialised nerve cell with dendrites, cell body, axon and terminals; transmits electrical impulses.
All nerves outside the CNS; subdivided into somatic and autonomic nervous systems.
Controls involuntary functions; sympathetic branch triggers fight-or-flight, parasympathetic restores rest-and-digest.
Outer layer of the brain divided into frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes with specialised functions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Peripheral nervous system”?
options: Brain and spinal cord; coordinates incoming sensory information and outgoing motor commands.
All nerves outside the CNS; subdivided into somatic and autonomic nervous systems.
Outer layer of the brain divided into frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes with specialised functions.
Controls involuntary functions; sympathetic branch triggers fight-or-flight, parasympathetic restores rest-and-digest.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cerebral cortex”?
options: Brain and spinal cord; coordinates incoming sensory information and outgoing motor commands.
Outer layer of the brain divided into frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes with specialised functions.
All nerves outside the CNS; subdivided into somatic and autonomic nervous systems.
Specialised nerve cell with dendrites, cell body, axon and terminals; transmits electrical impulses.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Synapse”?
options: Brain and spinal cord; coordinates incoming sensory information and outgoing motor commands.
Gap between neurons across which chemical neurotransmitters diffuse to signal.
Outer layer of the brain divided into frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes with specialised functions.
Specialised nerve cell with dendrites, cell body, axon and terminals; transmits electrical impulses.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Central nervous system”?
options: Brain and spinal cord; coordinates incoming sensory information and outgoing motor commands.
Controls involuntary functions; sympathetic branch triggers fight-or-flight, parasympathetic restores rest-and-digest.
Specialised nerve cell with dendrites, cell body, axon and terminals; transmits electrical impulses.
Outer layer of the brain divided into frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes with specialised functions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Neuron”?
options: Specialised nerve cell with dendrites, cell body, axon and terminals; transmits electrical impulses.
All nerves outside the CNS; subdivided into somatic and autonomic nervous systems.
Gap between neurons across which chemical neurotransmitters diffuse to signal.
Controls involuntary functions; sympathetic branch triggers fight-or-flight, parasympathetic restores rest-and-digest.

mcqs.q: How many lobes does each cerebral hemisphere have?
options: 4 lobes
5 lobes
2 lobes
3 lobes
